description: Access, modification, deletion, and auditing of files, folders, registry objects, and other securable objects.

source.note: Object access events require the 'Audit Object Access' policy and object SACLs to be configured.

4657.headline: A registry value was modified
4657.plain_english: A registry setting was changed. Registry entries control many Windows behaviours — attackers use them for persistence and to disable security features.
4657.technical_description: Security event 4657: registry value modified. ObjectName is the key path; OperationType indicates new/updated/deleted value.

where.Computer: Machine where the change was recorded

4657.why_it_matters: Registry is a common persistence and defence-evasion target.
suspicious_when: Changes to Run/RunOnce, Services, or Defender keys by an unusual process
what_to_do: Identify the process that made the change
Check whether the key is one attackers commonly modify

severity.high: Change to persistence or defence-evasion keys

4657.important_note: Review together with the process that made the change.

4661.headline: A handle to an object was requested
4661.plain_english: A program asked for access to a securable object (file, registry key, service, etc.). Shows what access was requested and whether it was granted.
4661.technical_description: Security event 4661: handle to an object requested (object type varies: file, key, service, etc.).
4661.why_it_matters: Shows attempted access to sensitive objects even when read-only.
suspicious_when: Unexpected process requesting handles to sensitive objects
what_to_do: Check whether the process is expected to access that object

severity.high: Access to LSASS, SAM, or other credential stores

4661.important_note: Handle request does not mean the access succeeded.

4662.headline: An operation was performed on an object
4662.plain_english: An operation was performed on a directory service (AD) object. Useful for tracking changes to users, groups, computers, and GPOs.
4662.technical_description: Security event 4662: operation performed on an AD object (typically on domain controllers). Properties show which attributes were accessed.

where.Computer: Domain controller that recorded the event

4662.why_it_matters: AD object changes include privilege escalation (e.g. adding to admin group, modifying ACLs, DCSync).
suspicious_when: Changes to ACLs on AD objects
what_to_do: If DCSync-related, treat as credential dumping

severity.high: Access matching known attack patterns (DCSync, LAPS password read)

4662.important_note: This is a broad event — the accessed Properties field is key.

4663.headline: An attempt was made to access an object
4663.plain_english: A program tried to access a specific file, folder, or registry key. Whether the access succeeded is recorded in the event.
4663.technical_description: Security event 4663: attempted access to a securable object (file, directory, registry key). Includes AccessMask and AccessList.
4663.why_it_matters: Shows who tried to read or modify a sensitive file — even if the attempt failed.
suspicious_when: Attempts to access files the user doesn't normally open
Access attempts on files like NTDS.dit, SAM, or shadow copies
what_to_do: Check whether the accessing account and process are expected
Correlate with subsequent 4663 events for the same account

severity.high: Access to sensitive files or correlated with other suspicious activity

4663.important_note: Depends entirely on which object was accessed — context matters.

4665.headline: An application client context was created
4665.plain_english: An application created a client authentication context. Used by applications doing custom authentication.
4665.technical_description: Security event 4665: application tried to create a client context (authentication-related).
4665.why_it_matters: Low-signal on its own; relevant when correlated with other authentication anomalies.
what_to_do: Confirm it should be doing custom auth

4666.headline: An application attempted an operation
4666.plain_english: An application performed a security-sensitive operation. Which operation depends on the event fields.
4666.technical_description: Security event 4666: application attempted a security operation (e.g. impersonation, token manipulation).
4666.why_it_matters: Some application operations (impersonation, token manipulation) are used by attackers.

severity.high: Impersonation or token manipulation by an unusual process

4666.important_note: Read the event's operation field for the specific action.

4667.headline: An application client context was deleted
4667.plain_english: An application cleaned up its client authentication context.
4667.technical_description: Security event 4667: application client context deleted.

4670.headline: Permissions on an object were changed
4670.plain_english: Someone changed the permissions on a file, folder, or object. This can grant new access — review what was changed and for whom.
4670.technical_description: Security event 4670: permissions on an object were changed. OriginalSecurityDescriptor and NewSecurityDescriptor show the change.
4670.why_it_matters: Permission changes are a common way to grant or persist access.
suspicious_when: Permissions opened up (Everyone/Full Control) on a sensitive object
Change performed by an unexpected account
what_to_do: Compare old and new security descriptors

severity.high: Weaker permissions on a sensitive object

4670.important_note: Always compare the old and new descriptors for the actual change.

implementation_notes.verified_field: Only display a plain-English explanation when `verified` is true.
